newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian demand cheers sub-continent sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian demand cheers sub-continent sentiment.

text.p: Strong wedding season demand pushed gold prices up in India while they remained firm in Pakistan despite low buying due to a Moslem mourning period, dealers said on Monday.
They said the revival in Indian demand cheered market sentiment in Dubai, the trading hub of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and a major re-export market for gold.
Dealers said they expected prices to remain firm on Bombay and mixed in Pakistan in the next few days.

On the Bombay bullion market, gold 24 carat rose 90 rupees to 4,840 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Monday. Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) gained 1,100 rupees to 56,600 rupees per piece in the same period.
"A firm trend in world prices pushed up the cost of imported gold and this affected fresh arrivals during the week, said Babubhai Jain, a leading bullion dealer in Bombay.
Gold prices in the world market rose to $349 per ounce from $340/341 dollars during the week.

Jain said a slight rise in the value of the dollar against the rupee during the week sent up the premia on special import licences (SILs), which are issued against export earnings and used for importing gold.
Premia on SILs rose to 13/13.25 percent from 12 percent during the week, Jain said.
Besides traders, Indian expatriates are also allowed to import up to 10 kgs of gold every six months, subject to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes.
Bullion dealer Bhayabhai Sanghvi said he would expect the prices to remain firm in the coming few days subject to some profit-taking at higher levels.
In Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi, dealers said they would expect gold prices to remain mixed because of poor demand in the Moslem mourning month of Muharram.

In Dubai, strong Indian demand for gold buoyed the bullion market in the week to Sunday, but traders said local retail interest had fallen sharply in the past few weeks since the end of a government-sponsored shopping promotion.
They said prices in Dubai had increased in line with a sharp rise in international bullion late in the week, spurred by a fall in the dollar and a COMEX options expiry.

"The local demand is a little down. There has been no recovery since the end of the Dubai shopping festival, but Indian demand for both gold and silver is great," said one dealer dominant in the Dubai-India precious metals trade.
The wedding season in India, which winds down in the next month or so, continues to fan demand, he said.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.82 Indian rupees, 40.43 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams) * Bombay prices May 12/5. Karachi and Dubai May 11/4.
